source.title: Universal Refusal Circuits Across LLMs: Cross-Model Transfer via Trajectory Replay and Concept-Basis Reconstruction

record.tranche_reason: The study tests refusal attenuation using transferred concept-basis directions and rank-one weight edits, rather than the original activation projection at every layer and position. It reports refusal and capability outcomes, making this a conceptual reproduction of intervention effects and a test of cross-model transfer.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for transferred edits, capability measures, and control edits. Spectral correlations, layer-alignment diagnostics, guard-ratio selections, and values used only to choose settings are not recorded as rows because they do not directly report refusal or capability outcomes. The paper's quoted prior-work claims are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study removes refusal with rank-one weight edits along a direction reconstructed from a donor's difference-in-means refusal vector. It reports refusal rates on 300 JailbreakBench prompts and GSM8K/MBPP capability across 8 donor→target pairs, with random-direction, wrong-map, unrelated-concept and no-guard controls. This is a different method aimed at the same question (V1, V2) and adds a cross-model transfer test (V6). It also has one reasoning-tuned target (V8).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that donor-derived concept recipes, replayed with DTW layer alignment and a weight-SVD guard, attenuate refusal across 8 pairs without target-side refusal supervision while preserving GSM8K/MBPP. They take this as support for a semantically universal refusal circuit. They frame ablation as a measurement tool and limit the claim to the tested families and CAR coverage.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses mean-difference concept atoms and a donor refusal direction, but reconstructs a recipe in a target concept basis, aligns a layer trajectory, applies rank-one weight edits to output projections, and adds an SVD guard. This differs from projecting one direction out of activations at every layer and position and does not test direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by target pair. The paper reports different refusal attenuation across targets and reports failures for random directions, permuted layer maps, and an unrelated concept recipe. Disabling the SVD guard is associated with capability collapse in the reported controls; selected guard ratio ρ is target-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: Donor and target refusal directions have correlated projections onto a 20-atom concept basis (ρ=0.865), and the same ridge coefficients reconstruct a working target direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal directions share a cross-model semantic composition over concept atoms (recipe invariance).

record.problems: The main capability assessment is limited to GSM8K and MBPP, with generation perplexity used for guard selection. The paper reports one frozen LLM judge for refusal scoring. Only four pairs receive deep control ablations, with additional control summaries for three pairs. GPT-OSS-20B is described as an anonymized internal research model. The text says all reported metrics include 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, but control-table deltas do not provide uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Activation-space directional ablation at every layer and position. Use of the target's own difference-in-means direction, since the target direction is reconstructed from donor concept coefficients. Capability beyond GSM8K and MBPP.
Whether the procedure matches community 'abliteration' as applied to public checkpoints. Edits are limited to attention O-proj with an SVD guard. Harmful-output quality was not evaluated.
Cross-language transfer and base-to-instruct transfer. Here transfer is of concept-recipe coefficients, not of the direction vector itself.
Whether GLM-4.6V actually reasons before answering under the greedy evaluation is not described. There is no analysis of reasoning traces, and there is only one reasoning-tuned model.
Not tested. There is no comparison of a single direction against multi-direction accounts.

missing.what: Compliance rates after the edit for all 8 pairs (0.96, 0.81, 0.92, 0.98, 0.99, 0.99, 0.88, 0.98). They show whether removing refusal yields full compliance rather than partial answers.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author preprint with no control-table uncertainty, although it claims all metrics have CIs. The 'GPT-OSS-20B' subject is declared an anonymized internal model. Section 9.3 is empty in the text, and Figure 5 is only described. Capability is measured only by GSM8K and MBPP. Rows r25 and r27 duplicate r4 and r5. The edit acts on a donor-reconstructed direction, not the target's own difference-in-means direction, so V1 evidence is indirect.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test adding the direction to induce refusals to harmless requests, nor does it ablate a single activation direction at every layer and position. Its intervention is a concept-reconstructed direction applied through rank-one weight edits along a mapped layer trajectory. Capability checks cover GSM8K and MBPP, not general capability broadly.

The study tests rank-one weight edits that attenuate refusal, but does not call the procedure abliteration or report that name as a distinct method. GPT-OSS-20B is described as an anonymized internal research model.
No jailbreak attack is tested as suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
The study proposes a semantic mixture over concept atoms but does not compare a single direction against affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts as competing explanations.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
The reported transfer is across the listed model pairs and regimes; the study does not test transfer across languages or from base to instruct models.
The study does not vary refusal-training methods or timing to test whether they determine the existence of a removable direction.
The study tests transfer to one model it calls reasoning-tuned, GLM-4.6V. It does not separately characterize reasoning traces or test a broader set of reasoning models.

relationships.condition: Guarded weight edits on 7 of 8 targets (Ministral-3-14B, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3-VL-2B, GLM-4.6V, GPT-OSS-20B and in-family pairs)
relationships.reason: Refusal falls to 0.00–0.08 and GSM8K/MBPP stay within about 0.5 points of baseline (r1-r3, r7-r24). Random, wrong-map and unrelated-concept controls barely move refusal (r28, r31, r34, r40, r42-r44).
relationships.display_finding: On seven of eight targets, refusal fell to 0.00–0.08 and GSM8K and MBPP remained within about 0.5 points of baseline, while random, wrong-map, and unrelated-concept controls barely changed refusal.

source_check.condition: Guarded weight edits on 7 of 8 targets (Ministral-3-14B, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3-VL-2B, GLM-4.6V, GPT-OSS-20B and in-family pairs)
source_check.reason: Table 2 confirms refusal 0.00-0.08 with GSM8K/MBPP within 0.5. Three caveats: the ablated direction is reconstructed, not the target's own; γ = 2.0 overshoots plain ablation; addition is untested. 'Barely move' overstates r43 (-12.4 pp).

relationships.condition: Qwen3-VL-8B→Ministral-3-3B pair; and all edits without the weight-SVD guard

relationships.display_finding: Ministral-3-3B retained refusal of 0.14, while edits without the guard removed refusal but caused capability collapse, including a 24.1-point GSM8K drop.
